status: measured model of the drill build (local workerd 2026-10-23; JS reserve from the long runs round2/f2, round2/plat1 and round2/steady-* under data/task-roots/testnet/workers-arena, stack from round2/stack1). The coordinator's model is measured at migration step 0 the same way.
page_bytes_source: WebAssembly page size, equal to the dlmalloc 0.2.12 system granularity
isolate_bytes_source: Cloudflare Workers limits: "128 MB per isolate", read as 10^6 bytes, the smaller of the two readings
js_reserve_bytes_source: measured JS high-water with its garbage backlog over long runs at the envelope shape (20,000 receipts), read through the inspector (Runtime.getHeapUsage: V8 committed heap + ArrayBuffer backing stores + embedder heap) after every invocation with collections forced every 100: 83,693,636 B in 5,000 steady package invocations (last new maximum at invocation 2,832, none over the final 2,168; round2/steady-package20k), 78,633,280 B in 5,000 streamed ones (flat from invocation 23; round2/steady-packagestream20k). Mixed workloads stayed below it: 83,544,676 B over 10,000 invocations, 3,000 small first, then shapes up to 26,000 (last new maximum at invocation 4,040; round2/plat1). Stated margin: one more invocation's JS need (8,480,236 B). The 80-invocation measurement this replaces (79,747,224 B at 26,000 receipts) was exceeded in the 1,000-invocation drill (90,508,484 B; round2/f2).
js_envelope_bytes_source: the per-invocation JS need at the envelope shape: request body 5,380,236 B + bundle sink 3,100,000 B at 20,000 receipts. The envelope is the largest measured shape whose JS reserve leaves a pool that holds the largest route and a quarantine budget at least as large: 26,000 receipts would need a long-run high-water of at most 88,205,460 B and reached 90,508,484 B (round2/f2), so it does not fit; 20,000 allows at most 96,909,844 B and measured 83,693,636 B. An invocation needing more is refused before it allocates.
glue_static_bytes_source: measured: 0 B of glue at idle in every drill scenario (the drill has no wasm-bindgen or workers-rs; run s1)
glue_ticket_bytes_source: measured: 1,008 B of glue at 22 tickets in flight (45.8 B per pending invocation's task box) in the abandonment scenario (run s1); stated margin: rounded up to the next power of two
glue_resident_bytes_source: the drill has no Durable Object instances
min_route_bytes_source: the drill route's CONTROL_BYTES, derived from serde_json's error footprint (drill/src/lib.rs CONTROL_FOOTPRINT)
largest_route_bytes_source: the drill package route at the envelope shape (20,000 receipts), from its admissions on wasm32: state page and control run 131,072 B + body block 5,439,488 B + entry vector block 1,966,080 B + bundle block 3,145,728 B = 163 pages (jobs/drill_model.py); witness: stats route_bound_exceeded stays 0 in the drill
stack_bytes_source: rustc 1.99.1 wasm32-unknown-unknown links the stack first with rust-lld's default -z stack-size=1048576: [__stack_low, __stack_high) = [0, 1,048,576) (scratch probe, 2026-10-31); the pool starts above static data, so the stack is outside every arena
stack_high_water_bytes_source: measured: the painted stack high-water (stats stack_high_water) of the drill arena build over every scenario (lane, package, packagestream, mixed, quarantine, abandon, trap, leakstep, jsenvelope): 2,848 to 2,944 B, including the 256-B unpainted guard (round2 run stack1, local workerd 2026-10-23). Stated margin: half the linked stack, so the clippy frame, future and stack-array thresholds are stack_bytes / 2 - high-water (build.rs)
